If the $VIX closed September at current levels, it would be the lowest monthly close since Nov 2024.

The $VIX is currently down 5 of the last 6 months. This is the longest such losing streak since Feb-Aug 2021.

The $VIX high water mark is 18.94 in September. This marks the lowest high water mark in a September since 2018.

The $VIX has seen at least 21.46 minimum in every October since 2018. With an average peak of 28.29.

Out of the remaining 3 months left in the year, October had the most red months vs. November and December dating back to 2009.

With Midterms, ongoing intensifying geopolitical tensions, sticky inflation, a hawkish Fed with likely another hike coming this year, uncertainty surrounding AI lately, October seems to be the ideal month we see a pullback.

I could be wrong. But I laid out the reasons.

Prepare.

Stocks are becoming more sensitive to sharp moves in the Treasury market:

The 30-day correlation between the ICE BofA MOVE Index and the S&P 500 is up to -0.58, its highest since mid-June.

The MOVE index, also called the "VIX of bonds," measures the yield volatility of 2Y, 5Y 10Y, and 30Y Treasuries.

This means rapid increases in bond volatility are now translating into larger declines in stock prices.

A similar phenomenon took place in March this year and in April 2025, when violent moves in the MOVE Index exacerbated market selloffs.

The index has now surged +8.0% over the last week, to 80.7 points, near its highest level since mid-May.

Bond volatility is again becoming a key driver of stocks.

Ben Horowitz and Erik Torenberg with Nas, Steve Stoute, and Grandmaster Caz on the Paid in Full Foundation

Caz penned rhymes that became Rapper's Delight. Even with his name in them, he got nothing.

The Paid in Full foundation honors the people who created hip-hop by making sure they're "paid in full," financially, spiritually, and culturally.

As Nas points out, money alone reads as a handout. So the grant comes attached to the honor. Each year at the foundation's Hip Hop Grandmaster Awards, pioneers are celebrated by the artists they inspired.

Caz ultimately received a five-year grant, bought a house, and left the projects. In his words: "The thing is the honor. The thing is putting you in the light that you deserve to be in."

Ben says he bought Paid in Full (the album) for $10 and got at least $5 million worth of value out of the record, with no way to pay it back.

The vision is paying the debt. Felicia Horowitz runs the foundation. She and Ben are matching donations 2.5 to 1, and every dollar goes to the artists.

Tokenized equities today are exactly where stablecoins were in 2019.

the first pmf is here. bringing equities onchain is just as obvious, simple, yet genius as bringing dollars onchain was back then. we've already seen the first growth spurt push us to the first few billion in onchain supply.

but zoom out and it's painfully obvious we're still incredibly early. an easy 100x in growth still ahead over the next few years.

here's where it gets interesting though:

stablecoin growth was slower, because we spent years operating in a completely different environment. one that mocked crypto, treated it with deep skepticism, and forced us to fight regulatory headwinds the whole way. one of the biggest catalysts, the GENIUS Act, only came last year, many years after the first pmf, and accelerated stablecoin significantly.

tokenized equities are positioned completely differently.

there's already massive institutional interest and adoption, and tokenized equities are an obvious, compelling fit for exactly that crowd. and just days ago the SEC issued its Innovation Exemption, explicitly allowing tokenized stocks to trade onchain, actively pushing this development forward instead of fighting it.

so I think tokenized equities are equally obvious with equally asymmetric upside as stablecoins in 2019. except this time it's going to move much, much faster.

one of the biggest opportunities forming in this space right now.

After nearly four years and three months, another one of the thousands of customers of my bank finally got his money back. Of course, had OCIF not done a favor for the IRS by illegally putting my completely solvent bank into receivership purely as a publicity stunt for the J5, so they could turn their failed Atlantis investigation into a fake success, he could have withdrawn all of his money over four years ago. 

Even if there had been a legitimate regulatory reason to shut down my bank, there was no need to appoint a Receiver to return deposits. I offered to liquidate the bank myself and personally guarantee the return of all deposits. But the corrupt OCIF Commissioner insisted on appointing a Receiver instead, creating an obvious conflict of interest: the longer he takes to return customers’ money, the more money he makes. He has already made over $1 million while taking more than four years to return a tiny fraction of the bank’s deposits—which I could have returned myself in full within a few weeks.

Below is a comment one customer just posted on a message board about his experience. It seems that he blames me for the agony he went through. My only mistake was opening a bank in Puerto Rico. I had no idea this would happen. I am the biggest victim of this crime. While I feel for the customers and am still doing my best to help them, blaming me lets the real culprits off the hook. All of the bad actors are government employees. The most corrupt and dishonest people in the world tend to work for governments. That is why government power needs to be kept to an absolute minimum. Power corrupts; absolute power corrupts absolutely.

A couple of weeks ago I finally got my money back, I opted︅ out. The process was incredibly long and arduous:

1) I was asked for the same⁠ documents multiple times, including bank statements and utility bills that I had already submitted in︆ due time.

2) I provided details for several bank accounts because the Receiver's bank couldn't︎ seem to process a standard wire transfer, and support kept telling me their attempts were‍ being rejected by my banks.

3) Eventually, out of sheer frustration, I set up additional⁢ accounts so they would run out of excuses.

Bear in mind I did the video⁤ interview in early April, yet it took five months to get my money back, involving︌ countless emails and even a few phone calls to the Receiver's office. I lost about︀ 8% of the original balance.

I can finally say I’ve put this nightmare behind me,⁣ but it is unacceptable it took so many months to execute just two bank transfers‌ (a test transfer and the final one).

The poor service, approximation and lack of communication︍ from Wigberto Lugo Mender were scandalous.

Thank you, Peter, for leading us into this agony,︊ much appreciated.

In 2006 I played WoW a lot

Now I couldn't afford official servers so we played on a hacked one, which was full of bugs (some really hilarious ones that made the game actually better imo)

Like there was not much PvP protection in usually protected areas, we could attack and gank anyone anywhere, no gloves...the GMs actually added some serious loot in strategic areas of each faction to incentivise players to organise PvP raids (and defend)

Naturally I focused on this real world PvP...I got quite decent at soloing PvPs, playing troll shaman and undead rogue (especially entertaining with slighgtly bugged stealth)...once I joined a spontaneous surprise raid on Stormwind

We swam from Stranglethorn to Westfall because Alliance was not expecting this angle. Something like 30 players, full on Omaha beach landing

We made it all the way to Stormwind to King Anduins throne room, when we heard there is big Allied dispatch coming to stop us. I came up with a plan for small group of us to pose as targets in the throne room, while the rest of us hid behind these big columns on the sides.

Allied defenders ran in the throne room without looking, emboldened by how small the decoy group was, and we jumped them from the sides and behind, surrounding them and making short work of them

I got offered to join the guild right after for my tactical prowess, climbed the ranks and somehow ended up becoming a Guild leader when the previous one got a new job and has much less time to play.

GMs on that server then teased a new unofficial addition - every guild will be able to buy their own fortress which will be spawned on the map in a neutral location of their choosing.

So I started collecting the gold from my guild members which was one of the biggest. We were also cornering some items in the auction to make more money and be the first guild to get the fortress.

But GMs got lazy, the fortress update never came and since I was the one collecting the gold, I became the richest player on that server on paper.

Ahhh good times

One thing that really stuck with me was reading Schumpeter during my first year of college. He wrote that capitalism’s greatest achievement wasn’t producing more silk stockings for queens, but making them affordable for factory girls.

That’s exactly what technology is doing today. Rich people have personal assistants managing their calendars and emails, chauffeurs driving them around, and people organizing their meals and daily lives.

Now everyone is getting AI agents and self-driving cars. Technology gradually turns the privileges of the rich into products available to everyone.
